items.q: A report of what our Beloved Prophet ﷺ said, did or approved.
The way of our Beloved Master ﷺ, which Muslims follow.
The most famous hadith book, by Imam al-Bukhari رحمة الله عليه.
The second most famous sahih book, by Imam Muslim رحمة الله عليه.
The two Sahih books together are called this.
The six main hadith books together are called this.
A collection of forty hadith by Imam al-Nawawi رحمة الله عليه.
The first hadith of Sahih al-Bukhari is about this.
The Companion who narrated the most hadith.
The Mother of the Believers who narrated the most hadith.
Our Beloved Prophet ﷺ said the best of you are those who learn this and teach it (paraphrased).
The hadith of the angel who asked about Islam, Iman and Ihsan is named after him.
The book of hadith by Imam Malik رحمة الله عليه.
The great Musnad was compiled by this Imam.
items.a: Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal رحمة الله عليه

items.q: Riyad al-Salihin, the "Gardens of the Righteous", was compiled by this scholar (meaning).
A Companion is someone who met our Beloved Prophet ﷺ as a believer and died as one. In Arabic, a Companion is called this.
The generation after the Companions.
The chain of narrators that carries a hadith.
Imam al-Bukhari رحمة الله عليه was born in this city of Central Asia.
Imam Muslim رحمة الله عليه was born in this city of Khurasan.
Our Beloved Prophet ﷺ said a Muslim is one from whose tongue and this other Muslims are safe.
Allah does not look at your bodies or forms, but at these.
Whoever Allah wants good for, He gives him understanding in this.
Whoever takes a path seeking knowledge, Allah makes easy for him a path to this.
"Convey from me, even if" this (meaning).
Seeking knowledge is an obligation on this person.
Imam al-Bukhari رحمة الله عليه died in this year.
Imam Muslim رحمة الله عليه died in this year.
The author of al-Sunan who was a student of Imam Ahmad, d. 275 AH / 889 CE.
items.a: Abu Dawud al-Sijistani رحمة الله عليه

items.q: The author of al-Jami' (al-Sunan), a student of al-Bukhari, d. 279 AH / 892 CE.
The author of al-Mujtaba (al-Sunan al-Sughra), d. 303 AH / 915 CE.
The author of al-Sunan from Qazwin, d. 273 AH / 887 CE.
The four books of Sunan are those of Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i and this scholar.
The famous commentary on Sahih al-Bukhari by Ibn Hajar al-'Asqalani رحمة الله عليه.
The commentary on Sahih Muslim by Imam al-Nawawi رحمة الله عليه.
Ibn Hajar al-'Asqalani رحمة الله عليه died in this year.
Imam al-Nawawi رحمة الله عليه died in this year.
Ibn Hajar's رحمة الله عليه short book of hadith on rulings.
The Companion and servant of our Beloved Master ﷺ for about ten years.
The Companion, son of the second caliph, known for following the Sunnah closely.
The Ansari Companion, narrator of many hadith, whose father fell at Uhud.
The Ansari Companion whose name was Sa'd ibn Malik, a narrator of many hadith.
Riyad al-Salihin and al-Arba'in were both written in this city.
The book by Imam al-Bukhari رحمة الله عليه on manners.
The book by al-Tirmidhi رحمة الله عليه on the qualities and character of our Beloved Prophet ﷺ.
The forty hadith of al-Nawawi رحمة الله عليه actually hold this many hadith.
The hadith of Jibril in Sahih Muslim is narrated by this Companion.
items.a: Our master 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (رِضْوَانُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ)

items.q: The last hadith of Sahih al-Bukhari speaks of two phrases light on the tongue and heavy on the scale: these.
items.a: Subhan Allah wa bi-hamdihi, Subhan Allah al-'Azim

items.q: "Avoid the seven destroyers," our Beloved Prophet ﷺ said; the first named is this (meaning).
The Companion who narrated "What is halal is clear and what is haram is clear" (meaning).
The hadith "None of you truly believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself" (meaning) is narrated by this Companion.
The hadith "Actions are by intentions" (meaning) is narrated by this caliph.
items.a: Our master 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (رِضْوَانُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ)

items.q: The hadith "Islam is built on five" (meaning) is narrated by this Companion.
The full title of Sahih al-Bukhari begins with these words.
Imam al-Bukhari رحمة الله عليه spent about this many years compiling his Sahih.
It is reported that Imam al-Bukhari رحمة الله عليه prayed this before writing each hadith in his Sahih (paraphrased).
The number of hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari with repeats, by the common count.
items.src: Fath al-Bari (numbering of Muhammad Fu'ad 'Abd al-Baqi)

items.q: The scholar who numbered the hadith of Sahih Muslim in the common modern edition.
The hadith book on prophetic prayers and remembrance by Imam al-Nawawi رحمة الله عليه.
The book of al-Hakim رحمة الله عليه that adds hadith he judged to meet the conditions of the two Sahihs.
The scholar who checked al-Mustadrak in his Talkhis.
The great Sunan of the Shafi'i scholar al-Bayhaqi رحمة الله عليه.
The three Mu'jams (large, middle, small) were compiled by this scholar.
The Sunan of al-Darimi رحمة الله عليه is also called this.
The Companion from the Daws tribe of Yemen who came to Madinah in 7 AH / 628 CE, the year of Khaybar.
Abu Hurayrah (رِضْوَانُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ) got his name, "father of the kitten", from his love of this (meaning).
The commentary on Sahih al-Bukhari by the Hanafi scholar Badr al-Din al-'Ayni رحمة الله عليه.
The commentary on Sahih al-Bukhari by al-Qastallani رحمة الله عليه.
The famous Maliki commentary on al-Muwatta' by Ibn 'Abd al-Barr رحمة الله عليه.
The transmission of al-Muwatta' most used today, through Yahya ibn Yahya al-Laythi رحمة الله عليه, came from this land.
By the common count, Abu Hurayrah (رِضْوَانُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ) narrated about this many hadith.
After Abu Hurayrah, the Companion with the most narrations by the common count.
Al-Shafi'i رحمة الله عليه said, before al-Bukhari's رحمة الله عليه time, that no book after the Book of Allah is more correct than this.
The Hanafi transmission of al-Muwatta' by the student of Abu Hanifah and Malik رحمة الله عليهما.
The famous commentary on Sunan Abi Dawud by al-Khattabi رحمة الله عليه.
The book of hadith on rulings by the Hanafi scholar al-Tahawi رحمة الله عليه.
The great Hanafi work by al-Zayla'i رحمة الله عليه that traces the hadith of al-Hidayah.
The book of Ibn Hajar رحمة الله عليه on the Companions.
The book of Ibn Hajar رحمة الله عليه on narrators, a summary of Tahdhib al-Kamal.
Tahdhib al-Kamal on the narrators of the six books was written by this scholar.
The book by al-Dhahabi رحمة الله عليه on criticised narrators.
Ibn Hajar's رحمة الله عليه one-line judgment on every narrator of the six books.
The book of Imam al-Bukhari رحمة الله عليه on the history of narrators.
The great Musnad of Imam Ahmad رحمة الله عليه holds roughly this many hadith.
The scholar who gathered the hadith of the Kutub Sittah and more into Jami' al-Usul.
items.a: Ibn al-Athir (Majd al-Din) رحمة الله عليه

items.q: The famous Shafi'i collection of hadith that arranges the hadith of earlier books by topic, by al-Baghawi رحمة الله عليه.
The expanded edition of Masabih al-Sunnah, by al-Khatib al-Tibrizi رحمة الله عليه.
The famous Hanafi commentary on Mishkat al-Masabih by Mulla 'Ali al-Qari رحمة الله عليه.
The book of al-Suyuti رحمة الله عليه listing short hadith in alphabetical order.
The commentary on al-Jami' al-Saghir by al-Munawi رحمة الله عليه.
The book of Qadi 'Iyad رحمة الله عليه on the rights and qualities of our Beloved Prophet ﷺ.
Qadi 'Iyad رحمة الله عليه was the judge of this city in Morocco.
The commentary on al-Arba'in al-Nawawiyyah by Ibn Hajar al-Haytami رحمة الله عليه.
The last hadith of al-Nawawi's رحمة الله عليه Forty is a hadith qudsi about this.
items.a: Forgiveness ("O son of Adam, as long as you call on Me")

items.q: Sahih al-Bukhari without repeats holds about this many connected hadith, by Ibn Hajar's رحمة الله عليه count.
The teacher whose wish for a short book of only sahih hadith moved al-Bukhari رحمة الله عليه to write his Sahih.
items.a: Ishaq ibn Rahawayh رحمة الله عليه

items.q: The scholar who first counted the Sunan of Ibn Majah among the six books.
items.a: Ibn Tahir al-Maqdisi رحمة الله عليه

items.q: Al-Bayhaqi's رحمة الله عليه book on the branches of faith.
Al-Bayhaqi's رحمة الله عليه book on the signs of prophethood.
Al-Haythami's رحمة الله عليه book gathering hadith beyond the six books from the Musnads and Mu'jams.
Al-Mundhiri's رحمة الله عليه book of hadith that encourage good and warn from evil.
The Imam of hadith called "Amir al-Mu'minin fil-Hadith", d. 161 AH / 778 CE.
The scholar of Basrah called the "commander of the believers in hadith", d. 160 AH / 776 CE (meaning).
items.a: Shu'bah ibn al-Hajjaj رحمة الله عليه

items.q: The Successor whom 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz رحمة الله عليه tasked with collecting hadith officially.
items.a: Ibn Shihab al-Zuhri رحمة الله عليه

items.q: The Umayyad caliph who ordered hadith to be written down officially, d. 101 AH / 720 CE.
The chain "Malik from Nafi' from Ibn 'Umar" (رِضْوَانُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِمَا) was called this by al-Bukhari رحمة الله عليه.
The early written page of hadith that Hammam ibn Munabbih رحمة الله عليه took from Abu Hurayrah (رِضْوَانُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ).
The Companion who wrote hadith in a page called al-Sadiqah.
The book by Ibn Abi Hatim رحمة الله عليه on praising and criticising narrators.
The early collection by 'Abd al-Razzaq al-San'ani رحمة الله عليه.
The great Musannaf of the Kufan scholar, d. 235 AH / 849 CE.
items.a: Ibn Abi Shaybah رحمة الله عليه

items.q: The Sahih of Ibn Khuzaymah رحمة الله عليه was compiled in this city.
The Sahih arranged by Ibn Balban, originally by this scholar of Bust.
items.src: al-Ihsan fi Taqrib Sahih Ibn Hibban

items.q: The book by al-Khatib al-Baghdadi رحمة الله عليه on the history of Baghdad and its scholars.
The great history of Damascus and its scholars by Ibn 'Asakir رحمة الله عليه.
The student of Ibn Hajar رحمة الله عليه who wrote al-Maqasid al-Hasanah on hadith common on people's tongues.
The book of al-'Ajluni رحمة الله عليه on sayings people think are hadith.
The Hanafi scholar of Cairo, author of Taj al-'Arus, who also wrote 'Uqud al-Jawahir al-Munifah on the evidence of Abu Hanifah رحمة الله عليه.
The famous Hanafi hadith book Kitab al-Athar was narrated from Abu Hanifah رحمة الله عليه by these two students.
items.a: Abu Yusuf and Muhammad al-Shaybani رحمة الله عليهما

items.q: The Shafi'i hadith master of Egypt who wrote al-Talkhis al-Habir.
items.a: Ibn Hajar al-'Asqalani رحمة الله عليه

items.q: In Jami' al-Usul, Ibn al-Athir رحمة الله عليه counted this book as the sixth instead of Sunan Ibn Majah.
Al-Muttaqi al-Hindi's رحمة الله عليه vast collection arranged from al-Suyuti's رحمة الله عليه works.
Al-Baghawi's رحمة الله عليه book of hadith with commentary on the Sunnah.
'Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak's رحمة الله عليه book of hadith on renouncing the world.
The teacher of al-Bukhari رحمة الله عليه, nicknamed "Commander of the Believers in hadith", famed for criticism of narrators.
